title: Persephone: The Descent
subtitle: A stolen daughter, a grieving mother, and why winter exists

narrativeBlocks.title: Picking flowers, gone
narrativeBlocks.body: Persephone, Demeter's daughter, is gathering flowers in a meadow when the earth splits open — Hades rises in his chariot, seizes her, and carries her screaming into the underworld to be his bride. Zeus, her father, has quietly permitted it.

narrativeBlocks.title: A mother who makes the world pay
narrativeBlocks.body: Demeter — goddess of grain — searches the earth nine days with torches. When she learns the truth, she doesn't rage at Hades; she simply stops working. Crops fail. Famine spreads. Humanity starves while a mother grieves — and the gods grow worried.

narrativeBlocks.title: The pomegranate seeds
narrativeBlocks.body: Zeus finally orders her return — but there's a catch. In the underworld Persephone ate pomegranate seeds (six in most versions), and anything eaten in the land of the dead binds you to it. She can't stay above forever.

narrativeBlocks.title: The compromise that makes seasons
narrativeBlocks.body: The settlement: a third of each year below, two-thirds above. When Persephone descends, Demeter grieves and the earth goes cold — autumn and winter. When she returns, her mother blooms the world — spring and summer. The whole cycle of seasons is a custody arrangement.

narrativeBlocks.title: The deepest mystery cult
narrativeBlocks.body: This myth anchored the Eleusinian Mysteries — the most important secret rites in the Greek world for a thousand years, promising initiates a better fate after death. The story isn't just weather: it's a promise that descent isn't the end.

quiz.prompt: How does Persephone end up in the underworld?

choices.text: She descends to rescue a companion
Demeter hides her there to spite Zeus
Hades abducts her while she gathers flowers — with Zeus's quiet permission — to be his bride
She falls through a cave gathering herbs

quiz.explanation: The abduction is arranged at the divine level — her mother's rage is justified.

quiz.prompt: Why can't Persephone stay above permanently?

choices.text: Hades has a legal claim by marriage
She is punished for the abduction
She ate pomegranate seeds in the underworld — food of the dead binds its eater to that realm

quiz.explanation: Underworld food is binding; the split year is the compromise that produces the seasons.
